chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Boston hotel engagement and the dispute with Moe Gale
summary: A "Dizzy" filled the tenor chair for four weeks in Boston; McRae pressed Moe Gale for more pay and a share, but Gale reneged.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I needed a tenor player, so Dizzy agreed to go up and play it with us. And Dizzy made the four weeks with us.
And after I played the four weeks, I couldn't come to any agreement with Moe Gale -- the agreement that we had on the band --
When we played the Apollo Theater that week, it was a deal that I was supposed to take up

with him that I wanted more money for the musicians, you know, because the band was making -- You must realize, the band was back where it was before Chick died. It was popular, and the only thing that was missing was Chick, you know. But they were making as much money or more because now that things had grown much bigger. Ella had grown into her own, you know. Her record was moving, "A Tisket A Tasket." So, Moe had made me a deal before -- when I took the band over there, that he would give me a piece of the action, you know. So he came back, he reneged on it.
